# Shared Native Reader Shell Defect

The Awtsmoos revealed beneath Chitas a wound shared by every Torah post reader road;
Awtsmoos.com must heal the common vessel once, so ordinary chapters and dynamic ranges carry the same load.

## Direct browser and HTTP evidence

A private 390px Chrome target reached the standard native post shell but no Chitas masthead or Torah body. The rendered page contained a server-template exception before `postLogic.js` could manifest the post. An ordinary Devarim chapter URL produced the identical exception.

The owner is `geelooy/heichelos/post/_awtsmoos.post.html`, which invokes `initial-content.html` with `$$sd` directly. On normal dynamic routes `$$sd` is not guaranteed to exist in that parent template scope. The server therefore throws `ReferenceError: $$sd is not defined` before the child template can apply its own safe default.

## Repair law

Rewrite the complete 108-line parent template. Preserve its reader shell and imports. Before invoking the initial-content partial, derive an object with `typeof $$sd !== "undefined" && $$sd ? $$sd : {}`. Pass that safe vessel into `$a`. Do not patch a line in place.

## Verification obligations

1. Ordinary Devarim chapter HTTP body contains no `thereWasAnAwtsmoosErrorHere` or `$$sd is not defined`.
2. Dynamic Chitas HTTP body has the same clean shell.
3. Private Chrome renders ordinary Devarim through `#realPost`.
4. Private Chrome renders native Chitas masthead and canonical Hebrew pesukim through the same reader.
5. No new runtime exceptions appear from the repaired template boundary.
